title: "Presentation"
subtitle: "An intro and four parts, each its own deck"

The talk runs in order: the intro, then Parts 1 to 4. Session 1, Foundations of AI Agent Evaluation, is Parts 1 and 2. Session 2, Practical Evaluation of AI Agents, is Parts 3 and 4.

Each part is its own slide deck and its own URL, so contributors can edit one section without rewriting the others. Decks inherit the same Reveal.js chrome from `presentations/_quarto.yml`. A part can override that in its own YAML when it needs a different theme or layout.

Inside a deck: open the slide list from the menu at the top left, move with the arrows or the left and right keys, and search the text of that deck. Escape returns to this site’s home page. The edge arrows fade when the pointer is still.

::: {#part-1 .part-card}
<span class="index">Part 1 · Session 1</span>

[AI Agents and Evaluation Challenges](01-agents-and-eval-challenges/){.card-title}

Presented by Terrence Szymanski. Why agents create value and risk, two LLM-judge examples, technical foundations (LLMs, generative AI and agents), and why agents need LLM judges.
:::

::: {#part-1g .part-card}
<span class="index">Part 1.G · Not in the talk</span>

[Graveyard](01g-graveyard/){.card-title}

Slides cut from Part 1, kept in full for organisers. To be deleted before the tutorial.
:::

::: {#part-2 .part-card}
<span class="index">Part 2 · Session 1</span>

[LLM-as-a-Judge Methods](02-llm-as-judge-methods/){.card-title}

Presented by Parvin Zarei Eskikand. Deterministic evaluation; LLM as a judge and its failure modes; rubrics, scales and prompt patterns; domain-specific criteria and human review.
:::

::: {#part-3 .part-card}
<span class="index">Part 3 · Session 2</span>

[Hands-on Agent Evaluation Exercise](03-hands-on-exercise/){.card-title}

Presented by Yelaman Abdullin. The exercise briefing: three rounds with one career assistant and five steps in every round. The app itself opens from [Hands-on](../hands-on/index.qmd).
:::

::: {#part-4 .part-card}
<span class="index">Part 4 · Session 2</span>

[Reliability, Limitations, and Future Directions](04-reliability-and-future/){.card-title}

Presented by Sara Mirabi. Reliability of the judge, what a judge score cannot tell you, and good practice and future directions.
:::
